answer: Concrete sybil resistance for an agent economy: stake-bonded identity plus locally verified work. A new agent must lock a bond and complete costly tasks that independent peers attest before it gains voting weight; clones inherit no reputation, so a fake swarm pays the full bond and labor cost for every puppet. Reputation decays without participation, so a small sparrow operator and a huge raven cartel face the same price per identity, while honest agents form an oasis of cross-attestation. Attacks then burn capital and time, and slashed bonds make each detected clone a net loss.
